unit.title: Nominalization
unit.subtitle: Turning verbs, adjectives and clauses into noun phrases

grammar.title: Turn anything into a noun
grammar.intro: Formal Spanish loves to nominalize — to package a quality, an action or a whole clause as a noun phrase. The neuter article lo abstracts adjectives and clauses (lo importante, lo que dijiste), el + infinitive names an activity (el atardecer), and deverbal nouns (la decisión, el crecimiento) replace bulky verb clauses. Mastering this makes your speech and writing more concise and sophisticated.

sections.heading: lo + adjective = the … thing / what is …
sections.body: The neuter article lo plus a masculine-singular adjective builds an abstract noun: lo bueno (the good thing / the upside), lo importante (what matters). It names a quality or idea, never a concrete object, so the adjective stays masculine singular even about feminine or plural referents.

sections.heading: lo de + noun and lo que + clause
sections.body: lo de + a noun or a time refers to a whole matter or affair: lo de ayer (that business from yesterday). lo que + a clause nominalizes an entire idea: lo que importa (what matters), lo que dijiste (what you said).

ex.en: I'm still thinking about that business from yesterday.

ex.es: Lo que me molesta es su tono.
ex.en: What bothers me is his tone.

sections.heading: el + infinitive = a full noun
sections.body: An infinitive introduced by el works as a complete noun — the name of an activity or concept: el deber (duty), el saber (knowledge), el atardecer (dusk). Like any noun it can take an adjective or a complement.

sections.heading: From verb to abstract noun
sections.body: Careful register prefers a deverbal noun to a full clause: instead of cuando decidieron, write tras la decisión. Frequent suffixes are -ción, -miento and -aje. Watch the gender: -ción nouns are feminine, most -miento/-aje nouns masculine.

ex.es: El crecimiento de la empresa sorprendió a todos.

ex.en: After the judge's decision, they appealed.

takeaways: lo + masculine-singular adjective = an abstract idea: lo bueno, lo importante.
lo de + noun = 'the matter of'; lo que + clause = 'what…'.
el + infinitive turns a verb into a noun: el deber, el atardecer.
Formal register favours deverbal nouns (-ción, -miento, -aje) over full clauses.

mistakes.why: The abstract 'the good thing' uses neuter lo, never la.
After lo the adjective stays masculine singular (lo importante), even when the verb is plural.
Deverbal nouns ending in -ción are feminine: la decisión.

exercises.no: An abstract quality takes neuter lo: “Lo importante”.

exercises.prompt: Tras la ___ del jurado, todos aplaudieron. (decidir)
exercises.prompt_en: After the jury's decision, everyone applauded.
exercises.no: The deverbal noun of decidir is “la decisión”.

exercises.prompt: Build: “What bothers me is his tone.”
exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! Lo que + cláusula → lo que me molesta.
exercises.no: “Lo que me molesta es su tono” — lo que nominalizes the whole idea.

exercises.hint: Neuter article for an abstract quality.
exercises.no: Use neuter lo for the abstract quality: “Lo difícil”.

exercises.prompt: Match each verb to its deverbal noun.

exercises.translation: What matters is not giving up.
exercises.no: It was: “Lo importante es no rendirse.” (What matters is not giving up.)

exercises.scenario: A friend brings up yesterday's argument 😕

lines.speaker: Marta
lines.es: ¿Sigues dándole vueltas a lo de ayer?
lines.en: Are you still mulling over that business from yesterday?

options.text: Sí, lo que más me duele es cómo lo dijo.
Sí, la que más me duele es cómo lo dijo.
Sí, el que más me duele es cómo lo dijo.

exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! Lo que nominalizes the abstract idea.
exercises.no: For an abstract idea use neuter lo que: “lo que más me duele”.

exercises.en: The good thing is that we learn.
exercises.no: Almost — tap “Hear it”, then match the sound of “Lo bueno es que aprendemos.”
